content:
rachel_cs: Nora from SkyFoundry reported an immediate spike of 429s during their first production traffic test after SDK init. They mentioned they see a 'warmup flood' pattern. Can infra/eng help triage?

nora_support: They run a fleet of 120 serverless workers that all call our /embed endpoint at boot to pre-warm caches. After deploy we got a cascade of 429s within 10s. Logs from one host:

nora_support: ```
2026-04-04T09:12:01Z INFO sdk: init complete
2026-04-04T09:12:01Z INFO request /v1/embeds start
2026-04-04T09:12:01Z WARN response 429 rate_limit_exceeded
2026-04-04T09:12:01Z INFO retrying (0) /v1/embeds
2026-04-04T09:12:01Z WARN response 429 rate_limit_exceeded
2026-04-04T09:12:02Z ERROR pool: exhausted, upstream unavailable
```

lee_sdk: Two common issues: (1) coordinated warmup without jitter, (2) SDK default preflight concurrency. What SDK version?

rachel_cs: They used sdk-js v2.1.0 from our quickstart.

lee_sdk: v2.1.0 had aggressive prefetch enabled for embeddings (preload=all) and no jitter on warmup. We've since changed defaults in v2.2.0.

omar_infra: From gateway side, we see a pattern of many short-lived connections from same key showing similar synching window. That trips our adaptive rate window and shifts some requests to return 429 quickly.

viktor_sre: Can you capture the source IPs and the exact timing? If they're all within <500ms windows that's the classic thundering-herd. Also check whether client's connection keepalive is disabled (causing many new TCPs).

nora_support: Captured — yes, most calls are within 200ms window and each worker does a fresh connection. They said keepalive is off for their environment.

lee_sdk: Quick mitigation steps we advise customers to try: enable keepalive/pinning, add randomized startup delay, or switch to batched warmup (one worker warms, others wait). Sample small patch we recommend:

lee_sdk: ```js
// recommended warmup helper
const jitter = () => Math.floor(Math.random()*1500);
setTimeout(() => sdk.embed(prewarmPayload), jitter());
// also set client options:
client.configure({maxConcurrentRequests: 6, keepAlive: true});
```

rachel_cs: Nora, can you try toggling keepalive and adding a small jitter to the warmup across the fleet?

nora_support: Will try — ETA 1h. For short term, can the gateway do anything to avoid immediate 429s so they don't cascade?

omar_infra: We can change the soft window of the adaptive limiter to be less aggressive for new keys for a short period. That reduces strict 429s during onboarding bursts. I'll open a config flag and roll it to canary.

deploybot: Deployment scheduled: 2026-04-04T10:30:00 UTC. sdkgateway adaptive limiter temp relax: true (canary 10% of hosts).

viktor_sre: Also plan to add consistent Retry-After header for transient limiter hits so clients can backoff properly.

lee_sdk: Also note that older SDKs ignored Retry-After. We'll add a runtime check to honor Retry-After and jitter further. Patch available in v2.2.1.

rachel_cs: Action items: (1) Nora will enable keepalive + jitter and retest (ETA 1h). (2) Omar to roll the adaptive limiter relax canary (ETA 10:30 UTC). (3) Lee to prepare SDK patch note and highlight warmup guidance in onboarding KB (ETA PR today). (4) Viktor to ensure Retry-After header present on limiter responses (ETA EOD).

nora_support: Update: after enabling keepalive and adding 0-1500ms jitter, warmup calls dropped under rate ceiling; only 2-3 429s observed during full fleet boot. Great improvement.

rachel_cs: Thanks everyone. We'll recap KB additions and include the sample code and checklist for serverless warmup.

kb_bot: New KB draft created: "Serverless warmup: avoid thundering-herd". Link: https://kb.redwood.ai/articles/2026/serverless-warmup.

rachel_cs: Closing this thread — reopen if any regression. :white_check_mark:
